rounds.text: Tejas Cargo India Ltd trades at a severe valuation disconnect that is not supported by its underlying financial reality, highlighted by a rich price-to-earnings ratio of 44.9x [E1] and a price-to-book multiple of 5.01x against a book value of ₹ 80.9 per share [E2]. This lofty pricing leaves no room for error, as evidenced by a discounted cash flow model placing intrinsic value at ₹ 200 per share—creating a negative margin of safety of -102.5% [E32, E33]—while a reverse DCF exposes that the current market price of ₹ 405 already demands an aggressive 19.7% earnings growth expectation [E2, E34]. Compounding these valuation risks, the company's financial structure shows escalating leverage with borrowings expanding to Rs 220 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 159 Cr previously, pushing the debt-to-equity ratio to 1.14x where debt exceeds net worth [E24, E26]. This aggressive debt accumulation directly hampers liquidity, resulting in a severe free cash flow deficit of Rs -50 Cr for March 2026 [E23] and contributing to a total lack of shareholder payouts through a 0.00% dividend yield [E4]. Furthermore, operational execution remains inconsistent, reflected in volatile yearly and quarterly operating margin trends over the last two periods [E19, E20], while institutional investors scale back their exposure amid negative money flows and domestic holdings dropping to zero [E29, E30, E31]. Conceded: [E8], [E9], [E10], [E14], [E21], [E22], [E28].
